questions.text: The two relays (which switch 230 V) sit 1 mm under the front board's low-voltage copper. Their plastic body insulates, but the maker does not say how far the live parts inside are from the top. How do we make that safe?
options: Add a 0.4 mm insulating sheet (polycarbonate or Formex, die-cut 62 x 40 mm) between the two boards (recommended: about 0.10 USD, stack goes from 28.2 to 28.6 mm of the 30 mm, standard practice for reinforced insulation through a solid layer)
Keep low-voltage copper off the front board above the relays (the front board loses about half its area; may not fit the parts at all)
Accept it for the 10 prototypes and settle it in the safety review before CE
questions.why: Requirement R8: 4 mm through air or a solid insulating layer between 230 V and anything touchable. The flat board check passes; this is the 3D stack.
